clue.text: Bows and scrapes to get marks of approval

parts.note: to scrape on a violin is to fiddle, so scrapes gives fiddles
ticks are the marks a teacher puts beside right answers

explanation.surface: A courtier bows and scrapes in the hope of earning approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bows and scrapes' reads as one phrase of servility, but 'Bows' alone is the definition: the sticks used to play fiddles.
explanation.definitionFit: The bow of a violin is the stick drawn across its strings, a literal fiddle-stick.

clue.text: Timber man out East becomes a writer

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for East is taken away from the timber man

parts.note: a forester looks after and fells trees for timber

explanation.surface: A lumberjack quits the East and takes up the pen.
explanation.walkthrough: E.M. Forster wrote A Passage to India and Howards End.
explanation.definitionFit: E.M. Forster was an English novelist, author of A Room with a View.

clue.text: Refuse to go through individual cases

definitions.meaning: in grammar, to list a noun's forms in each case, as in Latin lessons

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to work through every individual file.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an invitation is to decline it, and reciting a Latin noun's case endings is declining it.

clue.text: Recent appointment for judge, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the words are said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a judge who adjourns a case appoints a later day for it

explanation.surface: A newly made judicial appointment is the talk of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appointment' looks like a new job for a judge, but it is a date fixed by a judge: a later day, which spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day describes something of modern or recent times.

clue.text: Football clothes angrily torn off

definitions.meaning: a team's kit of shirt, shorts and socks
from the idiom 'tear a ... off someone', to scold them angrily

explanation.surface: A furious player rips off his football kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A football team's kit is called its strip, and an angry telling-off is 'tearing a strip off' someone.

clue.text: Originally a region lived in, by our ancestors

indicators.note: originally hints at the letters of a region being returned to some earlier arrangement

explanation.surface: Historians describe a region where our forebears first lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' rearranges A REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is the prehistoric period our ancestors lived through after the Bronze Age.

clue.text: A sauce boat at a higher, price

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
when prices are up they are higher than before

explanation.surface: A gravy boat is sold at an inflated price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' reads as the jug for gravy, but the words split: 'A sauce' is the definition and 'boat' is the ketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato ketchup is a thick sweet condiment poured over chips.

clue.text: Achievement of the single-minded, not quite mastery?

definitions.text: Achievement of the single-minded, not quite mastery?

parts.words: Achievement of the single-minded, not quite mastery?
parts.note: single-minded is read as minded to stay single, unmarried, and the degree that falls short of a master's is the first university degree

explanation.surface: A dedicated person achieves something just short of true mastery.
explanation.walkthrough: The state of being an unmarried man shares its name with the degree ranked below a master's.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying unmarried is the condition of a single man, and the first degree, below a master's, has the same title.

clue.text: Opportunity for a trick — put bed behind a tree

indicators.note: put asks us to place the bed into the month's name where its final letter was

parts.note: April Fools' Day, the first of April, is the traditional day for playing tricks
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone plans a prank: hide a bed behind a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: COT is put at the back of APRIL, replacing its final L; 'behind' says where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a fruit tree bearing small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: No entry in the duty-list: he's crowing

indicators.note: entry in tells us the letter for no is entered inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of who works when
O, the round zero, stands for nothing or no

explanation.surface: A gloating colleague finds nobody is on the rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No entry' looks like a sign, but No gives O and 'entry in' puts it inside ROSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is the farmyard bird famous for its morning cry.

clue.text: Restoring to life by taking to bed and swallowing the right cure revolting!

indicators.note: swallowing says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: lying down for a rest is resting

indicators.note: revolting, in the sense of rising up in turmoil, stirs the letters around

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An invalid takes to bed and gulps down a disgusting remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' shuffles R and CURE into URREC, which goes inside RESTING after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone from the dead is bringing them back to life.

clue.text: Wounded lion: the way to warn of the emergency

definitions.text: way to warn of the emergency

indicators.note: wounded suggests the words are damaged and put together again differently

explanation.surface: An injured lion: how do you raise the alarm?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wounded' rearranges LION and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct telephone link kept for urgent calls, like the Moscow-Washington line.

clue.text: Tells of twinges after exercise

indicators.note: after puts the twinges behind the exercise in the word

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
twinges of pain are aches

explanation.surface: Someone complains of pains following a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: To peach on someone is old slang for informing on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform against an accomplice is to peach on them, an old slang verb.

clue.text: Free to be at it, that's great

definitions.meaning: a prisoner on the loose is said to be at ..., so the word fills the gap after at

explanation.surface: Liberty to get stuck in feels wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped convict roams free 'at large', and something big is large.

clue.text: Boy, comes back to alleviate pet's illness

indicators.note: comes back tells us the boy's name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name
to temper is to soften or moderate

explanation.surface: A lad returns to soothe his sick dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns SID into DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a viral disease of dogs.

clue.text: Girl ordered her name to go in for the dance

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name

indicators.note: to go in tells us the name letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order

explanation.surface: A girl tells another her name is down to take part in the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside BADE to give BANDE after SARA.
explanation.definitionFit: The sarabande is a slow, stately dance in triple time.

clue.text: With speed, settler becomes a householder

parts.note: rate is speed, as in a rate of knots
one who settles a bill is the payer

explanation.surface: A quick-moving pioneer turns into a homeowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settler' looks like a colonist, but it is one who settles bills. Rates were the British local property tax paid by householders.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, the occupier of a property paid local rates, so the householder was the one billed.

clue.text: Theatrical knight speaking

parts.note: a knight said aloud is a night, and a famous Shakespeare comedy is a particular night of Christmas

explanation.surface: An actor with a knighthood delivers his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's comedy Twelfth Night supplies the word before a sound-alike of 'knight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play Twelfth Night takes its name from the last evening of Christmas festivities.

clue.text: Part company with philosopher there's no come-uppance

parts.note: Plato was the Greek philosopher

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Someone parts from a philosopher without getting their just deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part company' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a section of a company of soldiers. NO read upwards is ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a subdivision of an army company.

clue.text: Wait to start play

definitions.meaning: in tennis, to put the ball in play

explanation.surface: Hang on before the game begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter attends diners at table, and in tennis the first stroke of a point puts the ball in play.

clue.text: It is highly important to change lanes entering M1

indicators.note: entering puts one piece inside the other
change tells us the letters of lanes are rearranged

parts.note: the M1 is the British motorway, read as the letters MI

explanation.surface: It is vital to switch lanes when joining the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges LANES as SENAL, with MI inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is hugely influential, shaping what follows.

clue.text: Bird colony in Alsatia, for example

definitions.meaning: Alsatia was the slang name for Whitefriars in London, a lawless sanctuary slum

explanation.surface: A colony of birds lives in Alsace.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks nest together in colonies, and a squalid crowded tenement district was also called by the same name.

clue.text: Silly way to carve ham

indicators.note: silly way suggests the letters are taken in a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Someone carves a joint of ham the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat being carved, but it is the verb: to perform too theatrically. 'Silly way' rearranges TO and CARVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammy actor exaggerates every gesture, performing too theatrically.

clue.text: It has to go in the barn

definitions.text: It has to go in the barn

indicators.note: to go in places the first word inside the following one

explanation.surface: Something has to be stored in the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes inside THE. Tithes were church dues paid in produce, stored in great tithe barns.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of farm produce given to the church, kept in a tithe barn.

clue.text: Little 'craft evident when the boss goes in to bat

indicators.note: goes in to puts the boss inside the bat

parts.note: an umbo is the raised boss at the centre of a shield

explanation.surface: A small boat appears when the boss comes in to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager, but it is the knob on a shield, UMBO. A bumboat is a small boat selling goods to ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumboat is a small boat that carries provisions out to ships at anchor.

clue.text: Full-back comes to sort out warm-up

parts.note: a full-back is a defender, abbreviated DEF in team line-ups

indicators.note: sort out suggests putting the letters of sort into a new order

explanation.surface: A full-back arrives to organise the pre-match warm-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SORT as ROST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thawing frozen food means warming it until the ice melts.

clue.text: Name given to an extremely competitive material

parts.note: keen means eager, fiercely competitive

explanation.surface: A ruthless rival gets a reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: By coincidence, a mix-up results in a fatal quarrel

parts.note: chance is accident or coincidence
a medley is a mixture or jumble

explanation.surface: By sheer accident, a muddle leads to a deadly row.
explanation.walkthrough: Chance-medley is an old legal term for killing in a sudden fight.
explanation.definitionFit: In old law, a killing in a sudden brawl, without premeditation, was termed accidental homicide by this name.
